newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: British murder suspect died of asphyxiation.
newsitem.headline: British murder suspect died of asphyxiation.

text.p: British murder suspect Clifford Harris, found dead in the Swan River in Perth with a shirt tied round his neck, died of asphyxiation rather than drowning, police said on Friday.
Harris, a 62-year-old retired teacher, was due to be arrested in connection with the murder of a woman found in his abandoned pick-up truck on a farm in North Devon, England, Australian police said.
An autopsy revealed asphyxiation as the cause of death, and there were no suspicious circumstances, a police spokesman said.

Police would not comment further on how Harris died, although Australian media reported it was understood he had tied his shirt around his neck and tightened it with a stick before collapsing into the Western Australian river.
Harris was suspected of the murder of Janice Crompton, a 59-year-old art teacher, who lay for four days wrapped in a duvet tied with baler twine and placed in polythene bags in the rear of his truck.
A bee hive, thought to belong to Harris, an amateur bee-keeper, had been placed on the body. British police believe Crompton was beaten to death last week.
They are looking into the possibility that Harris and Crompton may have been having an affair.
Perth police said on Friday that Harris had been seen by local police on a routine patrol on Tuesday evening near riverside bushland.
"The police asked about his welfare," a spokesman said. "He said he had had a heavy meal and was walking it off."
The local police were not aware that Australian Federal Police were inquiring into Harris after receiving a request from Interpol to locate him from British authorities.
Harris' body was found on Wednesday morning.
Harris and his wife left Britain last week for a holiday in Australia where they have a son.
Federal police said Harris' wife, Margaret, had identified the body but was not a suspect in the murder of Crompton.
"We spoke to her on Wednesday but she was never in custody and she was free to go about her business," the spokesman said.
